text:
Incident Bot: ALERT: KV-cache total entries spiked 8x in us-east-1 replica pool, tail latency > 2s for generation requests, error rate up 4% – paging oncall
Tina Nguyen: On it. looking at dashboards now. paging Ravi and Kai.
Ravi Patel: I can take first triage. which customers are hit?
Incident Bot: Top mentions: cust-redwood-payments, cust-video-ads, cust-searchly. anomaly started ~10:12 UTC.
Tina Nguyen: Confirmed - continuous-batching upstream metric shows batch-window jumped from 20ms->200ms and per-key kv cache entries exploded.
Kai Chen: That sounds like cache amplification from long-lived prefixes. any recent deploys to batching logic?
Anna Park: We pushed batch-window optimizer yesterday (rollout 50%) and a new kv eviction heuristic. could be the optimizer increasing batch accumulation for some request patterns.
Ravi Patel: For immediate mitigation, recommend disabling continuous batching globally for us-east-1 while we investigate. we can do a canary first at 10% to validate.
Tina Nguyen: Agree. do we have per-customer overrides? CS wants to protect payments.
Marta Gomez (CS): Please prioritize cust-redwood-payments (high SLO + on-call on their side). they're seeing timeouts.
Kai Chen: We have customer flagging via ffsvc. Commands: `ffsvc toggle enable_continuous_batching --env=prod --region=us-east-1 --percent=10`
Ravi Patel: Running canary now. `ffsvc toggle enable_continuous_batching false --region=us-east-1 --percent=10`
Ravi Patel: Canary flip done. monitoring graphs… latency for canary nodes down to baseline.
Tina Nguyen: Good. let's escalate to 50% if stable for 3m. also open per-customer override for cust-redwood-payments and cust-video-ads to 0% immediately.
Kai Chen: `ffsvc override enable_continuous_batching --customer=cust-redwood-payments --value=false` -> applied. `cust-video-ads` done as well.
Anna Park: Patch ready to limit max entries per key and add a tighter LRU cap: PR #4512. It should reduce worst-case blowups without full disable.
Tina Nguyen: Can we hotpatch just the eviction params without rolling back optimizer?
Anna Park: Yes — it's a config-only change with zero downtime. patch command: `kubectl -n runtime set configmap kv-params --from-literal=max_entries_per_key=128 --from-literal=eviction_batch=50` then rollout restart canaries.
Ravi Patel: I'm going to promote canary disable from 10%->50%. executing: `ffsvc toggle ... --percent=50`
Ravi Patel: 50% done. metrics stable for 2m. error rate trending down.
Marta Gomez (CS): FYI cust-redwood-payments reporting recovery after override. thanks.
Tina Nguyen: Anna, please deploy the config patch to canary nodes (10 pods) first. monitor memory/latency.
Anna Park: Deploying now. `kubectl rollout restart deployment/runtime-canary`
Kai Chen: While that's rolling, I'm going to pin a per-customer manual throttle for cust-searchly — they have many small high-cardinality requests that triggered amplifier. `routectl set-throttle --customer=cust-searchly --qps=20`
Ravi Patel: Patch canary looks good — cache entries per key down by ~90% on canary pods. no regressions on throughput.
Tina Nguyen: Proceed to global config rollout after 5m of stable canary. keep continuous batching flag at 50% until global done.
Anna Park: Global config roll started. applying to all runtime pools. `kubectl apply -f configs/kv-params.yaml`
Incident Bot: Deploy event: config/kv-params applied by Anna Park at 10:28 UTC; tracking rollout.
Ravi Patel: Global rollout complete. monitoring shows normalized kv cache sizes, and tail latency back under 300ms across us-east-1.
Marta Gomez (CS): Great — sending customer recovery notes to cust-redwood-payments and cust-video-ads. can we confirm no data loss?
Kai Chen: No data loss; this was eviction and batching behavior only. logs show some bounded request throttling for cust-searchly which we manually limited.
Tina Nguyen: Next steps: 1) revert continuous batching flag to default gradual rollout after we validate additional telemetry for 1 hour, 2) follow-up PR to add better heuristics for high-cardinality prefixes, 3) postmortem and customer impact summary for CS.
Anna Park: I'll open the PR for heuristic improvements and schedule a canary test harness to simulate high-cardinality traffic.
Ravi Patel: I'm going to hand off monitoring and post-incident checks to Kai for the next shift. Kai, you ok to own the 1h watch and then start the postmortem doc?
Kai Chen: Yep I'll own it. starting a perf-check script that will run every 5m: `scripts/perf_check.sh --region=us-east-1 --metrics=kv_entries,latency,error_rate`
Tina Nguyen: Handoff noted. I'm going offline for a bit but reachable via phone if needed. thanks all for fast moves. :thumbsup: 
Incident Bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: Root cause narrowed to batch-window optimizer interacting with high-cardinality request patterns, triggering kv cache amplification. Status: mitigated via per-customer overrides + config hotfix.
Marta Gomez (CS): Sending recovery note to customers. I'll compile any customer-facing timeline and escalate if any legal/finance questions come up.
Kai Chen: I'll draft the postmortem and include suggested guardrails: circuit-breaker for kv cache growth, per-customer SLO alerts, and more conservative default for batch accumulation.
Ravi Patel: Thanks team. leaving notes for next oncall in #eng-oncall as well.
Tina Nguyen: End of thread — please add any follow-ups to the postmortem ticket assigned to ENG-6323.
